title: Index source-bound cheat capabilities without enabling them
changes: Assess bounded CodeBreaker provenance against its explicitly linked master and report source-specific decoded plans, one-shot footprints, unresolved sources, unsupported formats and unevaluated limits in CLI and local summaries.
Show localized capability and ROM-context reasons in the read-only menu while preserving imported entries and leaving all cheats disabled and unverified.
validation: Frozen offline Windows GNU release and test builds passed with 1914 source files, four overlays, no compiler messages or source drift. Wine passed 12 focused cheat tests; one local-catalog test remained intentionally ignored.

Seven EUR source plans matched their explicit source/master inspections, with the original catalog unchanged. A synthetic Wine/Xvfb menu displayed the ROM-context requirement with frame, clock and guest state unchanged; session pins and catalog remained exact. The first GUI setup failed on a helper path; a corrected fresh attempt passed and closed.
limitations: Source decoding assumes the linked master and does not verify device behavior, ROM bytes, checksum, native hooks or gameplay. Manual one-shot requires explicit selection and runtime preflight; maintenance, toggles and full device/ROM capability coverage remain open.
Native Windows, Linux and physical controller paths were not exercised. The frozen validation excluded independent concurrent uncommitted changes.
